title: Perihelion server-library auth checkpoint
content:
This Perihelion pass tightened the line between the page shell and the real hosted archive. The goal was to keep local-folder experiments flexible while making sure the server-backed library still behaves like a protected archive.

What changed:

  • Separate archive auth flag: the Python API now has an explicit PERIHELION_SERVER_LIBRARY_REQUIRE_AUTH setting so server-backed folders, thumbnails, shares, downloads, and direct file URLs can stay locked independently of the broader page shell.
  • Frontend and backend aligned: Peri's auth-status response now exposes that server-library rule directly, and the React app uses it when deciding whether Server Library mode should be available.
  • Deliberate no-split on Vite: we checked the current production bundle during this pass and intentionally left it unsplit because it still builds cleanly at a reasonable size with no chunk warning.

Why this matters: Perihelion now has a cleaner future-facing model for two different jobs in one app. The browser-side local folder workflow can keep evolving without weakening the hosted archive, and the archive itself remains protected from manual asset requests by logged-out visitors.
